Sends a message over an addon comm channel.
``` result = C_ChatInfo . SendAddonMessage ( prefix , message [, chatType [, target ]]) = C_ChatInfo . SendAddonMessageLogged ```
prefix string \- Message prefix, can be used as your addon identifier; at most 16 characters. message string \- Text to send, at most 255 characters.

All characters (decimal ID 1-255) are permissible except NULL (ASCII 0). chatType string ? `= "PARTY"` \- The addon channel to send to. target string | number ? \- The player name or custom channel number receiving the message for `"WHISPER"` or `"CHANNEL"` chatTypes.

Recipients must register a prefix using C\_ChatInfo.RegisterAddonMessagePrefix () to receive its messages via CHAT\_MSG\_ADDON . This prefix can be max **16 characters** long and it's recommended to use the addon name if possible so other authors can easily see which addon a registered prefix belongs to.
result Enum.SendAddonMessageResult \- Result code indicating if the message has been enqueued by the API for submission.
This does not mean that the message has yet been sent, and may still be subject to any server-side throttling.

Communications on all chat types are subject to a per-prefix throttle.
Each registered prefix is given an allowance of 10 addon messages that can be sent. Each message sent on a prefix reduces this allowance by 1.
If the allowance reaches zero, further attempts to send messages on the same prefix will fail, returning `Enum.SendAddonMessageResult.AddonMessageThrottle` to the caller.
Each prefix regains its allowance at a rate of 1 message per second, up to the original maximum of 10 messages.
Additionally, if too much data is being sent simultaneously on separate prefixes then the client **may be disconnected** .

SendAddonMessageLogged Addons transmitting user-generated content should use this API so recipients can report violations of the [Code of Conduct](https://us.battle.net/support/en/article/42673) . Fires CHAT\_MSG\_ADDON\_LOGGED when receiving messages sent via this function. _The message has to be plain text for the game masters to read it._ Moreover, the messages will silently fail to be sent if it contains an unsupported non-printable character. Some amount of metadata is tolerated, but should be kept as minimal as possible to keep the messages readable for Blizzard's game masters. [[ 3 ]]() This function has been introduced as a solution to growing issues of harassment and doxxing via addon communications, where players would use addons to send content against the terms of service to other players (roleplaying addons are particularly affected as they offer a free form canvas to share a RP profiles). As regular addon messages are not logged they cannot be seen by game master, they had no way to act upon this content. With a duration of 0 ms, the earliest the callback will be called is on the next frame.
C\_Timer.After() is generally more efficient than using an Animation or OnUpdate script.
In contrast, the new C\_Timer system uses a standard heap implementation.
It’s only doing work when the timer is created or destroyed (and even then, that work is fairly minimal).
The one case where you’re better off not using the new C\_Timer system is when you have a ticker with a very short period – something that’s going to fire every couple frames.

Details Will return globalstring `UNKNOWNOBJECT` "Unknown Entity" if called before the unit in question has been fully loaded into the world.
The unit name will change if the unit is under the effects of [[ Lifegiving Seed ]](/wiki/Lifegiving_Seed) or a similar effect, but `UnitNameUnmodified()` is unaffected by this.
`UnitFullName()` is equivalent with `UnitName()` except it will always return `realm` if used with the "player" UnitId.

If `showServerName` is true and the queried unit is from a different server, then the return value will include the unit's name appended by a dash and the normalized realm name.
If `showServerName` is false, then `FOREIGN_SERVER_LABEL` `" (*)"` will be appended to units from _coalesced_ realms. Units from the player's own realm or Connected Realms get no additional suffix.

Sends a message over an addon comm channel.
``` result = C_ChatInfo . SendAddonMessage ( prefix , message [, chatType [, target ]]) = C_ChatInfo . SendAddonMessageLogged ```
prefix string \- Message prefix, can be used as your addon identifier; at most 16 characters. message string \- Text to send, at most 255 characters.

All characters (decimal ID 1-255) are permissible except NULL (ASCII 0). chatType string ? `= "PARTY"` \- The addon channel to send to. target string | number ? \- The player name or custom channel number receiving the message for `"WHISPER"` or `"CHANNEL"` chatTypes.

Recipients must register a prefix using C\_ChatInfo.RegisterAddonMessagePrefix () to receive its messages via CHAT\_MSG\_ADDON . This prefix can be max **16 characters** long and it's recommended to use the addon name if possible so other authors can easily see which addon a registered prefix belongs to.
result Enum.SendAddonMessageResult \- Result code indicating if the message has been enqueued by the API for submission.
This does not mean that the message has yet been sent, and may still be subject to any server-side throttling.

Only works for players on the same or any connected realms. Use player name as target argument. Prints a _"Player is offline."_ system message if the target is offline. |
|"CHANNEL" |✔️ |❌ |Addon message to a custom chat channel. Use channel number as target argument. Disabled on Classic to prevent players communicating over custom chat channels. |
Communications on all chat types are subject to a per-prefix throttle.
Each registered prefix is given an allowance of 10 addon messages that can be sent. Each message sent on a prefix reduces this allowance by 1.
If the allowance reaches zero, further attempts to send messages on the same prefix will fail, returning `Enum.SendAddonMessageResult.AddonMessageThrottle` to the caller.
Each prefix regains its allowance at a rate of 1 message per second, up to the original maximum of 10 messages.
Additionally, if too much data is being sent simultaneously on separate prefixes then the client **may be disconnected** .

Prior to Patch 11.0.0 , Blizzard has provided a deprecation wrapper for this API that shifts the result code to the second return position. A forward-compatible way to reliably access the enum return value is to use a negative select index to grab the last return value.

Fires CHAT\_MSG\_ADDON\_LOGGED when receiving messages sent via this function. _The message has to be plain text for the game masters to read it._ Moreover, the messages will silently fail to be sent if it contains an unsupported non-printable character. content.executive_summary:
- **Release state**: Blizzard schedules the WoW: Forever beta for **2026-09-17 through 2026-10-21** and the launch for **2026-11-04** [executive_summary[0]] [1]. Treat all Forever runtime claims as unverified until the beta client can be inspected.
- **Official identity**: The evidence identifies WoW: Forever as a Blizzard-distributed World of Warcraft product delivered through Battle.net, not as a documented community emulator or private server [executive_summary[0]] [1][executive_summary[1]] [4]. Do not use similarly named third-party projects as technical evidence.
- **Launcher and access**: The official product page requires a Battle.net account and Battle.net desktop app, and the product page states that a WoW subscription or game time is required [executive_summary[0]] [1]. Test with the official Battle.net installation rather than a separate launcher.
- **Runtime boundary**: Blizzard's public product copy describes new content and upgraded graphics but does not publish a Forever build number, Lua version, XML/FrameXML contract, addon path, TOC parser, taint model, or API list [executive_summary[0]] [1]. Do not assume that the TBC value `## Interface: 20506` will load.
- **Classic baseline**: The public API references document the requested core functions across several official game types, including BCC Anniversary 2.5.6 (68184), Classic Era 1.15.9 (69109), Mists Classic 5.5.4 (68077), and mainline 12.1.5 (69594) [executive_summary[2]] [12]. This is a useful control group, not proof about Forever.
- **Church's risk profile**: Church of Beef uses ordinary UI, SavedVariables, guild roster, target, timer, duel-event, and addon-message dependencies rather than combat automation. That makes a compatibility port plausible, but only if Forever retains the relevant standard runtime and guild transport.
- **Networking risk**: The official addon-message contract imposes a 16-character prefix, 255-character message limit, result codes, per-prefix throttling, and target restrictions [executive_summary[3]] [11]. Keep the existing small-payload design and test every return code in Forever.
- **Identity risk**: Standard WoW account-level SavedVariables and per-character SavedVariables use different account, realm, and character paths [executive_summary[4]] [13][executive_summary[5]] [6]. Forever's account, realm, connected-realm, and guild identity model is not published, so guild data must be namespaced only after observing actual values.
- **Ecosystem evidence**: The Blizzard forum material located is user discussion, not a Blizzard addon specification. Claims about Retail-like restrictions, built-in meters, or future addon behavior are explicitly community claims [executive_summary[6]] [3]. There is no verified Forever-specific porting guide or compatibility release in the evidence gathered.
content.1_official_identity_operator_launcher_an:
Blizzard's own product page describes WoW: Forever as a reimagining of World of Warcraft's first age, with new or expanded zones, gameplay enhancements, and upgraded graphics [1_official_identity_operator_launcher_and_legal_boundary[0]] [1]. The official Battle.net product page presents editions, launch information, and access requirements [1_official_identity_operator_launcher_and_legal_boundary[1]] [4]. This is strong evidence that the product is distributed inside Blizzard's World of Warcraft and Battle.net ecosystem.

The public pages do not name a separate Forever studio, independent operator, emulator framework, or third-party backend. The safest factual wording is therefore: **WoW: Forever is an official Blizzard/Battle.net product; the specific engineering team, client fork, server implementation, and addon subsystem are not disclosed in the pages reviewed.** Its official distribution is evidence against treating it as a community private server, but it does not by itself prove whether the client is technically a modified official client, a new client built on Blizzard technology, or another implementation.

The official access model is Battle.net account plus the Battle.net desktop app, with a WoW subscription or game time required [1_official_identity_operator_launcher_and_legal_boundary[0]] [1]. No separate Forever launcher is identified in the primary material. The official page exposes links for Facebook, X, YouTube, Reddit, and Instagram, but no Forever-specific Discord link is shown in that link set [1_official_identity_operator_launcher_and_legal_boundary[0]] [1]. A generic World of Warcraft community Discord exists, but it is not evidence of an official Forever developer or support server [1_official_identity_operator_launcher_and_legal_boundary[2]] [17].

The legal conclusion must remain narrow. Blizzard publishes an end-user license agreement [1_official_identity_operator_launcher_and_legal_boundary[3]] [18], and the product is accessed through Blizzard's commercial account system. The sources reviewed do not provide a Forever-specific addon policy, API promise, or statement that community addons are guaranteed, supported, or prohibited. Therefore this report makes no legal opinion about Church of Beef. Before distribution, check the current Blizzard terms and any beta-specific rules, and do not interpret the absence of an addon statement as permission or prohibition.
content.2_client_era_build_engine_filesystem_and:
### What is confirmed and what is not

The product is presented as a new or expanded World of Warcraft experience rather than as a documented TBC client. Blizzard's wording about the first age and reimagined content does not identify an expansion-era API baseline [2_client_era_build_engine_filesystem_and_toc[0]] [1]. No primary source located by the cutoff gives a Forever executable build, interface number, renderer or engine name, client branch, server emulator status, or release archive. The scheduled beta is therefore the first reliable opportunity to answer those questions.

For comparison, the current public API material identifies official game-type baselines, including BCC Anniversary 2.5.6 (68184) and Classic Era 1.15.9 (69109) [2_client_era_build_engine_filesystem_and_toc[1]] [12]. The requested `## Interface: 20506` is the Church of Beef TBC target supplied in the brief. It must not be copied to Forever until the beta client reports an interface value or accepts the TOC during an actual load test.

### Official WoW baseline

In standard WoW packaging, the TOC file is mandatory, its filename matches the addon folder, and metadata uses `## Directive: Value` syntax [2_client_era_build_engine_filesystem_and_toc[2]] [6]. The standard layout is therefore conceptually:

```text
<Game install>\Interface\AddOns\ChurchOfBeef\ChurchOfBeef.toc
```

The `## Interface` directive identifies the WoW version for which the addon was made; an older value is treated as out of date, and an omitted value is also treated as out of date [2_client_era_build_engine_filesystem_and_toc[2]] [6]. Multiple interface values can be comma-delimited [2_client_era_build_engine_filesystem_and_toc[2]] [6]. These are official-client conventions, not confirmed Forever conventions.

Standard account-level SavedVariables are stored below the account SavedVariables directory, while `SavedVariablesPerCharacter` uses the account, realm, and character hierarchy [2_client_era_build_engine_filesystem_and_toc[2]] [6]. The documented general form is `WTF/Account/<account>/SavedVariables/<addon>.lua` for account-wide data and a realm/character-specific SavedVariables directory for per-character data [2_client_era_build_engine_filesystem_and_toc[3]] [13]. Forever may preserve this structure, rename its game-type root, or change its account and realm identifiers; the actual beta installation must decide the port.

The TOC documentation also lists modern suffix conventions such as `_TBC`, `_Wrath`, `_Cata`, `_Classic`, and `_Mainline`, while noting that the legacy `-BCC` convention is no longer supported in Classic Anniversary [2_client_era_build_engine_filesystem_and_toc[2]] [6]. Do not infer from those official suffixes that Forever accepts any of them. Use the exact suffix and interface value accepted by the beta client.
content.3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison:
### Runtime status

No Forever primary source confirms Lua 5.1, XML loading, FrameXML compatibility, CreateFrame behavior, widget set, secure templates, taint propagation, event registration, slash-command registration, minimap-button support, or either the modern `C_AddOns.LoadAddOn` or legacy `LoadAddOn` path. The user addon is written for Lua 5.1, but that is a Church of Beef requirement, not evidence about the unreleased Forever executable.

Official Classic material does establish a useful control: Classic uses the modern WoW API model, including secure execution and taint concepts [3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[0]] [19]. WoW's event model delivers named events to registered frames through an `OnEvent` handler [3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[1]] [20]. Whether Forever inherits those mechanisms must be tested, not inferred from its marketing language.

The required API comparison is:

| Platform | Evidence in the reviewed official API material | Church of Beef implication |
|---|---|---|
| Classic Era | `UnitIsInMyGuild`, `GetPlayerInfoByGUID`, `C_Timer`, and `UnitName` pages list Classic Era coverage [3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[2]] [14][3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[3]] [15][3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[4]] [7][3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[5]] [16]. | Strong control target for standard Classic behavior. |
| TBC Anniversary | The API references list BCC Anniversary 2.5.6 (68184), and the required function pages list BCC Anniversary coverage [3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[6]] [12][3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[2]] [14][3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[3]] [15][3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[4]] [7]. | This is the closest documented baseline to the requested `20506` addon. |
| Wrath/Cata Classic | The TOC reference recognizes Wrath and Cata naming conventions, but the evidence gathered does not provide a separate complete function matrix for those clients [3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[7]] [6]. | Do not claim exact availability or return signatures without a client-specific check. |
| Retail/Mainline | The same API references list mainline 12.1.5 (69594) and document the shared functions [3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[6]] [12][3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[2]] [14][3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[3]] [15][3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[4]] [7][3_addon_runtime_and_api_comparison[5]] [16]. | Retail documentation is useful for semantics but is not proof of Forever compatibility. |
| WoW: Forever | No official Forever build, API manifest, TOC specification, or runtime documentation was found before the scheduled beta. | All runtime cells remain unknown; no Forever-only API is confirmed. |

There is no confirmed Forever-only API or custom Lua library in the evidence. In particular, do not add a compatibility dependency merely because an unofficial search result uses the name WOWF.
content.4_church_of_beef_dependency_matrix:
The following separates the exact standard behavior that can be used as a control from the behavior that must be measured in Forever.

| Church dependency | Official baseline | Forever status and test |
|---|---|---|
| `GetGuildRosterInfo` | The documented return tuple includes name, rank, level, class, zone, notes, online state, and GUID; the related roster refresh event is `GUILD_ROSTER_UPDATE` [4_church_of_beef_dependency_matrix[0]] [12]. | Unknown. Confirm tuple positions, GUID presence, roster refresh timing, and whether a roster request is needed. |
| `UnitIsInMyGuild` | It returns whether a unit is in the player's guild, is documented for Classic Era, BCC Anniversary, Mists Classic, and mainline, and is permitted only when untainted [4_church_of_beef_dependency_matrix[1]] [14]. | Unknown. Test with player, target, party, and an unloaded or absent unit. |
| `UnitName` and `UnitGUID` | `UnitName` returns a name and possibly a realm, with a nil realm for a same-realm unit in the documented model [4_church_of_beef_dependency_matrix[2]] [16]. | `UnitName` return shape and `UnitGUID` availability must be tested in Forever, especially for cross-realm names. |
| `GetPlayerInfoByGUID` | It accepts a GUID and can return localized and English class/race information, sex, name, and normalized realm; it can return nothing when information is unavailable [4_church_of_beef_dependency_matrix[3]] [15]. | Unknown. Test player, target, guild-roster, offline, and foreign-realm GUIDs. |
| `C_Timer.After` | The documented function schedules a callback after a delay and is listed for Classic-family game types [4_church_of_beef_dependency_matrix[4]] [7]. | Unknown. Verify callback timing and whether the function is available before the first frame update. |
| Addon messaging | Prefix registration and send APIs have explicit limits, targets, return results, and throttles [4_church_of_beef_dependency_matrix[5]] [11]. | Unknown. Test prefix registration, GUILD send, `CHAT_MSG_ADDON`, failure results, and reconnect behavior. |
| Duel detection | Official event references include `DUEL_REQUESTED` and `DUEL_FINISHED` [4_church_of_beef_dependency_matrix[6]] [9][4_church_of_beef_dependency_matrix[7]] [21]. | Unknown. Capture actual event arguments and test request, accepted duel, cancellation, completion, out-of-bounds, and logout cases. |
| CreateFrame, XML, slash commands, minimap button | These are standard addon concepts, but no Forever-specific primary source confirms them. | Unknown. First test should load a minimal frame, register one event, create one slash command, and display one button without secure actions. |

The roster and GUID rows matter for the guild-scoped and duel-scoped parts of Church of Beef. Do not replace a missing Forever roster API with an invented wrapper or assume that a player name is a globally unique identity.
content.5_networking_guild_messages_and_identity:
The official addon-message model uses `C_ChatInfo.RegisterAddonMessagePrefix` before communication and `C_ChatInfo.SendAddonMessage` for sending. The documented send contract limits prefixes to 16 characters and messages to 255 characters, queues the message rather than guaranteeing immediate transmission, and returns an enumeration describing the result [5_networking_guild_messages_and_identity[0]] [11]. The documented targets include `GUILD`, `OFFICER`, `PARTY`, `RAID`, `INSTANCE_CHAT`, and `WHISPER`; `CHANNEL` is disabled on Classic in the reference history [5_networking_guild_messages_and_identity[0]] [11].

The throttle is material to the port. The reference documents an allowance of 10 messages per prefix, recovery of one allowance per second, and a warning that flooding through separate prefixes can disconnect a client [5_networking_guild_messages_and_identity[0]] [11]. Church of Beef should keep one stable prefix, short messages, explicit sequencing, and a queue or backoff if the existing implementation does not already have one. It should treat the send result as meaningful rather than assuming that a call means delivery.

The public history records API changes across eras, including the move to `C_ChatInfo` in BfA, Classic addon-message throttling changes, removal of the Classic `CHANNEL` target, and later changes from Boolean results to result codes [5_networking_guild_messages_and_identity[0]] [11]. This is why a Retail API page cannot be used as a complete TBC or Forever contract. The beta test must record the exact function names, event payloads, return values, target restrictions, and throttle behavior.

Cross-realm guild messaging, connected-realm identity, custom server channels, whisper routing, and whether Forever has a separate transport are unknown. Do not assume that a guild message reaches every character with the same guild name, or that a realm name is stable across account sessions.

The standard SavedVariables hierarchy is account-level versus realm/character-level [5_networking_guild_messages_and_identity[1]] [13][5_networking_guild_messages_and_identity[2]] [6]. Blizzard's Forever page separately describes an in-game Legacy system that grants account-wide benefits [5_networking_guild_messages_and_identity[3]] [1]. That gameplay statement does not establish that addon SavedVariables are account-wide across realms, nor that a Forever account identifier matches the official WoW account-directory convention. For Church of Beef, retain the account-level database but add a schema namespace based on observed realm and guild identifiers, and store a stable character or GUID key only after confirming its availability and privacy behavior.
content.6_existing_addon_ecosystem_and_breaking_:
No verified Forever-specific release or developer guide for WeakAuras, ElvUI, Questie, Details, or Church of Beef was found in the reviewed primary material. The Blizzard forum topic located is useful as a record of community uncertainty, not as documentation. Users asked about addon status [6_existing_addon_ecosystem_and_breaking_difference_evidence[0]] [3], speculated that addon support might resemble Retail with similar restrictions [6_existing_addon_ecosystem_and_breaking_difference_evidence[0]] [3], and discussed possible API limitations [6_existing_addon_ecosystem_and_breaking_difference_evidence[0]] [3]. Another user reported a built-in damage meter seen in a short preview, but that is a user report rather than a published client specification [6_existing_addon_ecosystem_and_breaking_difference_evidence[0]] [3].

The practical breaking risks are therefore known only by category:

1. **Load failure**: Forever could reject `20506`, reject a legacy TOC suffix, or use a different addon directory.
2. **Runtime mismatch**: Lua, XML, FrameXML widgets, or event payloads could differ even if the addon loads.
3. **API namespace mismatch**: `C_ChatInfo`, `C_AddOns`, legacy aliases, or roster APIs could be absent, renamed, or restricted.
4. **Transport mismatch**: guild addon messages could be disabled, limited to a different target, routed differently, or subject to different limits.
5. **Identity mismatch**: account, realm, guild, and GUID values could not match the standard SavedVariables assumptions.
6. **Security mismatch**: secure templates or taint rules could be stricter, even though Church of Beef does not automate combat.

None of those possibilities is a confirmed Forever behavior. No custom library, custom API, successful port, or failed port should be reported as fact until it is backed by a beta client capture, an official Blizzard statement, or a reproducible public source tied to the actual Forever client.
content.7_beta_validation_plan_and_minimal_port_:
Use the first beta build as a controlled compatibility experiment, with the TBC Anniversary client as the control. Record the client version, interface number, install root, and exact addon folder before changing Church of Beef.

**Phase 1: loader and storage**

- Place a minimal addon in the observed `Interface\AddOns` location.
- Test the existing folder/TOC naming convention and each candidate interface value, including the value reported by the beta rather than assuming `20506`.
- Confirm Lua file order, XML loading if used, `ADDON_LOADED`, slash registration, and a simple `CreateFrame` display.
- Write an account-level SavedVariables value, exit normally, restart, and confirm the value is restored. Record the actual account, realm, character, and game-type directory names.

**Phase 2: required API probe**

- Record the existence and return values of `GetGuildRosterInfo`, `UnitIsInMyGuild`, `UnitName`, `UnitGUID`, `GetPlayerInfoByGUID`, and `C_Timer.After`.
- Trigger `GUILD_ROSTER_UPDATE` and verify the roster GUID and online fields.
- Test player, target, guild member, offline, same-realm, and other-realm cases separately.
- Capture `DUEL_REQUESTED` and `DUEL_FINISHED` arguments for a sanctioned test duel, including cancellation and boundary cases. Do not infer a duel state from combat events or automate any action.

**Phase 3: messaging**

- Register the Church prefix and send a deliberately small `GUILD` message to a second test character.
- Verify `CHAT_MSG_ADDON`, sender identity, target identity, duplicate handling, reconnect behavior, and the exact send result.
- Test payloads near the documented 255-character limit only after the small case works. Measure actual throttling rather than relying on the official Classic values.
- Confirm that the channel is guild-scoped and does not silently become cross-realm or custom-server traffic.

**Phase 4: packaging and ecosystem**

Keep the TBC package unchanged as a control and create a separate Forever package only after the beta's interface and TOC behavior are known. Prefer the existing `C_ChatInfo` path when it is present, but do not add a fallback until the fallback function is observed and its return semantics are tested. Avoid dynamic loading, secure action templates, combat decisions, and Retail-only APIs unless a specific Forever test proves a dependency is necessary.

A conditional go decision is justified only if the addon loads, account-level data persists, frames and slash commands work, guild messages travel in both directions, roster/GUID lookups work, timers fire, and duel events expose enough information for the sanctioned-duel workflow. If any of those gates fails, the correct result is a documented compatibility block, not a guessed shim.
content.synthesis:
The evidence supports three different technical postures. **Official Classic Era and TBC Anniversary** provide the strongest control because their API references expose standard roster, GUID, timer, and guild-membership behavior, and the addon-message reference exposes concrete limits and throttling. **Retail/Mainline** provides useful modern namespace and security semantics but has a different release history and should not be treated as a drop-in contract. **WoW: Forever** is currently a product identity and release schedule, not a documented addon target: its official pages establish the commercial Battle.net boundary and new-game positioning, but not the implementation details required for a port [synthesis[0]] [1].

The main tension is between a familiar addon design and an unfamiliar platform. Church of Beef is comparatively low risk because it uses standard UI and communication facilities and does not automate combat. The same facilities are also the highest-risk boundary because guild transport, roster identity, duel events, and SavedVariables paths are exactly the parts Blizzard has not documented for Forever. The product's account-wide gameplay rewards create a second possible confusion: account-wide game progression does not prove account-wide addon storage [synthesis[0]] [1].

Accordingly, the right current answer is **port-ready in principle, not certified in fact**. Preserve the TBC implementation, avoid speculative Forever APIs, and make the beta probe the source of truth. There are currently no confirmed Forever-only APIs, no confirmed custom Lua libraries, no confirmed addon path, no confirmed interface/build number, and no confirmed Forever-specific addon ecosystem. Any stronger claim would go beyond the evidence available at the 2026-09-14 cutoff.
